mainTopic: עירוב תבשילין, רבי אליעזר's יום טוב lecture, and how to divide יום טוב
overview: The משנה teaches that when יום טוב falls on Friday, you may not cook on יום טוב just for שבת. You may still keep יום טוב leftovers for שבת, or make an עירוב תבשילין before יום טוב and rely on it. בית שמאי require two dishes and בית הלל one, and the עירוב works as long as any of it remains. The גמרא finds a source in 'זכור את יום השבת', and a תנא finds a hint in 'את אשר תאפו אפו'. רבא says the purpose of the עירוב is to save a good portion for שבת. רב אשי says it reminds people not to cook on יום טוב for another day. Next comes a story: רבי אליעזר criticized people who left his יום טוב lecture early to go eat. This leads to his מחלוקת with רבי יהושע about whether the day may be given entirely to ה' or must be split in half. The גמרא then explains phrases from the פסוק in נחמיה, including that הקב"ה repays money borrowed to honor the day, and adds a teaching about the אדר tree. The amud ends as רב תחליפא begins a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No cooking on יום טוב for שבת, but leftovers are fine
steps.stepSummary: When יום טוב falls on Friday, you may not cook on יום טוב with the plan of cooking for שבת. You may cook for יום טוב, and whatever is left over may be eaten on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יום טוב falls on Friday, a person may not start cooking on יום טוב for שבת. But he may cook for יום טוב, and if food is left over, it stays for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the basic rule: cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for יום טוב itself, not for the next day, שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is בתחלה, 'from the outset.' Cooking with the purpose of feeding שבת is forbidden. If he honestly cooked for יום טוב and food happened to remain, he may use it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset, as the plan from the start

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: A Festival that falls on Shabbat eve —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל בַּתְּחִלָּה מִיּוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: one may not cook from the outset on the Festival for Shabbat.
But he may cook for the Festival,
and if he left some over, he left it over for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking on יום טוב for שבת from the outset is forbidden; leftovers from יום טוב cooking may be used on שבת.

steps.title: Preparing a dish before יום טוב to rely on for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the solution: prepare a cooked dish before יום טוב and rely on it to cook on יום טוב for שבת. This is the עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person makes a cooked dish on the day before יום טוב and relies on it to cook for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents the way to permit cooking for שבת on יום טוב: a dish made before the holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This dish acts as if the שבת cooking already began before יום טוב. Once it is set aside, he may 'lean on it' and continue cooking for שבת on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'joining of cooked dishes' that permits cooking on יום טוב for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The עירוב תבשילין is not the food you eat on שבת in place of cooking. It is a dish made before יום טוב that lets you cook more for שבת on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: And he makes a cooked dish on the Festival eve,
and relies on it for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way around the restriction from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dish prepared before יום טוב allows one to cook on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the practice of making an עירוב תבשילין whenever יום טוב falls on Friday.

steps.title: How many dishes: בית שמאי versus בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי require two dishes for the עירוב, while בית הלל say one is enough. Both agree that a fish with an egg on it counts as two dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say you need two cooked dishes, and בית הלל say one dish. They agree that a fish with an egg on top counts as two dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה records a disagreement about the size of the עירוב and then a point both sides accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל are lenient and accept a single dish. The 'agreement' tells us that two foods cooked together, a fish and the egg on it, satisfy even בית שמאי's demand for two.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes,
and Beit Hillel say: one dish.
And they agree about a fish and the egg that is on it,
that they are two dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how much food the עירוב from step 2 requires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require two dishes, בית הלל one; a fish with an egg on it counts as two.

steps.title: If the עירוב is eaten or lost
steps.stepSummary: If the עירוב dish was eaten or lost, one may no longer cook for שבת on its basis. If any small amount remains, he may still rely on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate it or it was lost, he may not start cooking based on it. If even a tiny bit is left, he may rely on it for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by explaining that the עירוב must still exist when the cooking for שבת is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission depends on the dish being there. Once it is gone completely, the permission ends. But כל שהוא, any amount at all, is enough to keep it working.
steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב is on Friday: no cooking for שבת on its own, but an עירוב תבשילין made beforehand allows it. בית הלל need only one dish, and as long as any of it remains, it works.

phrases.english: If he ate it or it was lost —
he may not cook on its basis from the outset.
And if he left any amount of it,
he may rely on it for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit on the עירוב: it must still exist.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A completely eaten or lost עירוב no longer permits cooking; any remnant keeps it valid.

steps.title: What is the source for these rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where the law of עירוב תבשילין comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking for a source. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave rules without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what basis there is for forbidding cooking for שבת on יום טוב without an עירוב, and for the עירוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the law of עירוב תבשילין and the ban on cooking for שבת without it.

steps.title: שמואל: remember שבת when another day may make you forget it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל cites 'זכור את יום השבת לקדשו' and explains: remember שבת because of another day, יום טוב, that could cause it to be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says, 'Remember the שבת day to keep it holy.' Remember it because of another day that comes to make it forgotten.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by reading a פסוק as the reason for the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב falls on Friday, a person busy with the holiday might forget to prepare properly for שבת. The עירוב makes him deliberately set aside food for שבת before יום טוב, so שבת is remembered.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a sage of the גמרא

phrases.english: Shmuel said: As the verse states:
"Remember the Shabbat day, to keep it holy,"
Remember it, because of another day that comes to make it forgotten.
phrases.notes: The 'other day' is the יום טוב right before שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זכור את יום השבת' teaches us to guard שבת from being forgotten because of a יום טוב before it, which is the reason for the עירוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the purpose of עירוב תבשילין is to keep שבת in mind when יום טוב comes right before it.

steps.title: What is the purpose of the עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חכמים made the עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the purpose of the עירוב תבשילין is. This short question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל already gave a source from a פסוק, but that does not tell us what problem the עירוב solves. The גמרא now wants the reasoning behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish set aside before יום טוב so one may cook on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did חכמים make the עירוב at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the עירוב (שמואל) to its purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose behind the תקנה of עירוב תבשילין.

steps.title: רבא: so a good portion is saved for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the עירוב makes a person set aside a good portion for שבת as well as for יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: So that he will pick out a nice portion for שבת and a nice portion for יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first reason. The עירוב makes sure a person does not use up all the best food on יום טוב and leave nothing special for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the עירוב is about honoring שבת. Preparing a dish ahead of time guarantees that שבת gets its own good food.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the first to give a reason here
That he will choose or pick out

phrases.english: Rava said:
So that he will pick out a nice portion for Shabbat
and a nice portion for Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב is for the honor of שבת, so a choice portion is set aside for it.

steps.title: רב אשי: so people know not to cook on יום טוב for another day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the עירוב teaches people that one may not bake on יום טוב for שבת, and certainly not for a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: So that people will say, 'One may not bake on יום טוב for שבת,' and all the more so not on יום טוב for a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different reason. The עירוב is a reminder that cooking on יום טוב for another day is normally not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the עירוב protects the honor of יום טוב. Because people see that even cooking for שבת needs a special step, they will conclude by קל וחומר that cooking for a weekday is surely forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the second reason
All the more so; reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ אֵין אוֹפִין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: So that people will say: One may not bake on Yom Tov for Shabbat,
and all the more so not on Yom Tov for a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב reminds people that cooking on יום טוב for another day is forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה says ערב יום טוב, which fits רב אשי but not רבא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires the עירוב to be made on ערב יום טוב. That fits רב אשי, but for רבא even making it on יום טוב should work.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'One makes a cooked dish on ערב יום טוב and relies on it for שבת.' This works well for רב אשי, who said the reason is so people will say one may not bake on יום טוב for שבת. That is why on ערב יום טוב it works and on יום טוב it does not. But according to רבא, why specifically ערב יום טוב? Even on יום טוב it should be fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the wording of the משנה to challenge רבא. If the point is only to set aside good food for שבת, that could be done on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the reminder only works if the dish is made before יום טוב, because cooking on יום טוב for שבת is exactly what is supposed to look forbidden. For רבא, the goal of saving a nice portion would be reached even on יום טוב, so the משנה's word 'מערב יום טוב' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one view), but...

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
One makes a cooked dish on the day before Yom Tov
and relies on it to cook for Shabbat.
It works well according to Rav Ashi,
who said the reason is so that people will say:
One may not bake on Yom Tov for Shabbat.
That is why on the day before Yom Tov, yes,
but on Yom Tov itself, no.
But according to Rava,
why specifically on the day before Yom Tov?
Even on Yom Tov it should also work!
phrases.notes: Setting aside a nice portion for שבת could happen on יום טוב too.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: עוֹשֶׂה תַּבְשִׁיל מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְסוֹמֵךְ עָלָיו לַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two reasons of steps 8 and 9 against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires ערב יום טוב, but רבא's goal of saving a nice portion would be met even on יום טוב.

steps.title: Answer for רבא: a גזירה so he does not forget
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that by רבא's reason it could work on יום טוב, but חכמים required ערב יום טוב so a person would not end up forgetting to make it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But חכמים made a גזירה, in case he is careless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It admits his reason alone would allow making it on יום טוב, but חכמים added a rule to make it beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement of ערב יום טוב is not part of רבא's basic reason. It is an extra safeguard: if people waited until יום טוב, they might forget and never make it, and שבת would be left without a nice portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by חכמים
Lest he be careless or negligent

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the עירוב is for the honor of שבת (a nice portion), and it must be made on ערב יום טוב only as a גזירה in case he forgets. רב אשי: the עירוב is for the honor of יום טוב, teaching that one may not cook on יום טוב for another day.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
but it is a decree, in case he is careless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יִפְשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 on behalf of רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the logic, then adds a separate rabbinic גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבא, the עירוב could be made even on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could have been, but חכמים required ערב יום טוב so a person would not forget to make it.

steps.title: A Torah hint for עירוב תבשילין from the מן
steps.stepSummary: A תנא brings the פסוק 'bake what you will bake' as the source. From it רבי אליעזר learns that one may bake or cook on יום טוב for שבת only by building on food already prepared. חכמים used this as a Torah support for עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא brings the source from this פסוק: 'What you will bake, bake, and what you will cook, cook.' From here רבי אליעזר said: you may bake only on top of what is already baked, and cook only on top of what is already cooked. From here חכמים found support in the Torah for עירובי תבשילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source, a פסוק, that hints to the idea of עירוב תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was said on ערב שבת about the מן, telling the people to prepare their food ahead of time. רבי אליעזר reads this to mean that cooking for שבת should start from something already prepared beforehand. That is exactly what the עירוב is: a dish made before יום טוב, which the rest of the cooking for שבת 'rests on.'

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה
Leaned on; found support (a hint) in a פסוק
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Found support' does not mean the Torah itself requires an עירוב. We already saw that חכמים made this rule; the פסוק is a hint they leaned on.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea behind the עירוב: cooking for שבת on יום טוב must be a continuation of something already started before יום טוב.

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the source for עירוב תבשילין.

phrases.english: "What you will bake, bake,
and what you will cook, cook,"
From here Rabbi Eliezer said:
One may bake only on top of what is already baked,
and one may cook only on top of what is already cooked.
From here the Sages found support
for the joining of cooked foods from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for עירוב תבשילין, answering the 'מנא הני מילי' question of step 5 differently from שמואל's 'זכור' in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baking and cooking on יום טוב for שבת must build on food already prepared before; this is the Torah hint for עירוב תבשילין.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's lecture and the first three groups who left
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי אליעזר taught הלכות יום טוב all day. As the first three groups left, he described them as owners of big jugs, barrels, and pitchers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: It happened that רבי אליעזר sat and taught the laws of יום טוב the whole day. When the first group left, he said: These are owners of huge jugs. When a second group left, he said: These are owners of barrels. When a third group left, he said: These are owners of pitchers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about רבי אליעזר teaching on יום טוב while people kept leaving early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group that left was going home to eat and drink. רבי אליעזר names each group by a wine container, and each container is smaller than the one before, matching how long they stayed before leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: A story / an incident that happened

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer
who was sitting and lecturing

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ בְּהִלְכוֹת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: the entire day about the laws of the Festival.
The first group left; he said:
These are owners of huge jugs.
phrases.notes: He means they are rushing home to big feasts with lots of wine.

phrases.english: A second group; he said:
These are owners of barrels.
A third group; he said:
These are owners of pitchers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story, still about רבי אליעזר and food on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר criticized those who left his יום טוב lecture early to go eat.

steps.title: The fourth, fifth, and sixth groups leave
steps.stepSummary: The groups keep leaving, and רבי אליעזר names them by smaller containers: jars, then cups. When the sixth group starts leaving, he calls them owners of a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a fourth group left, he said: These are owners of jars. When a fifth group left, he said: These are owners of cups. When a sixth group began to leave, he said: These are owners of a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues as more groups leave, and רבי אליעזר's comments get sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The containers keep shrinking, down to a cup. By the sixth group he no longer names a container at all; he calls them 'owners of a curse,' showing how upset he is that the בית מדרש is emptying out.

phrases.english: A fourth group; he said:
These are owners of jars.
A fifth group; he said:
These are owners of cups.
A sixth group began to leave; he said:
These are owners of a curse.
phrases.notes: He means they barely have anything waiting at home, so why are they leaving?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּת רְבִיעִית, אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי לְגִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story with the later groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving Torah study for less and less reason earns harsher criticism, up to 'owners of a curse.'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reassures the students who stayed
steps.stepSummary: The students who stayed get scared that he means them. He tells them his words were about those who left, who give up eternal life for temporary life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He looked at the students, and their faces began to change color. He said to them: My sons, I am not talking about you, but about those who left, who leave behind eternal life and busy themselves with temporary life.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues as רבי אליעזר explains who his criticism was really aimed at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students who stayed feared the 'curse' comment was about them. רבי אליעזר makes clear the problem was with those who left: they traded Torah study, which is eternal, for eating, which only lasts a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Looked at; turned his eyes to
Their faces changed (from fear or shame)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's message: Torah is חיי עולם and eating is חיי שעה, so leaving Torah study early just to eat is a poor trade.

phrases.english: He cast his eyes upon the students,
and their faces began to change.
He said to them: My sons,
I am not saying this about you,
but about those who left,
who abandon eternal life
and engage in temporary life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by explaining whom רבי אליעזר's criticism was aimed at.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The criticism was for those who leave Torah (eternal life) to go eat (temporary life), not for the students who stayed.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר sends the remaining students off with a blessing
steps.stepSummary: When the students who stayed finally leave, רבי אליעזר tells them to go eat, drink, and rejoice, quoting a פסוק from נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they were leaving, he said to them: 'Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to anyone who has nothing ready, for the day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, for the joy of ה' is your strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. After teaching all day, רבי אליעזר sends the loyal students home to enjoy the festive meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He criticized those who left early, but he praises these students. Once the learning is finished, he tells them to go and feast. So he is not against eating on יום טוב. He is against leaving the learning in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: their departure, when they were leaving

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's complaint was only about leaving the learning early. When the learning was done, he sent his students off to celebrate.

phrases.english: At the time of their departure, he said to them:
"Go, eat rich foods
and drink sweet drinks
and send portions to whoever has nothing prepared
for the day is holy to our Lord
and do not be sad
for the joy of ה' is your strength."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in Step 13. It shows how רבי אליעזר treated the students who stayed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a full day of learning, the students are sent to celebrate יום טוב with food and drink.

steps.title: Isn't festive eating itself a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's line about 'temporary life' and challenges it: שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה, so how can it count as temporary life?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'They leave eternal life and busy themselves with temporary life.' But the joy of יום טוב is a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי אליעזר's harsh words from Step 15 and asks a question about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר called going off to eat 'temporary life,' as if it had no spiritual value. But eating to rejoice on יום טוב is a מצוה, and a מצוה is part of eternal life. So why does he criticize it?

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Master said', a way of quoting a ברייתא just cited

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's lecture from the steps before.

phrases.english: that they leave eternal life
and busy themselves with temporary life
But the joy of the festival —
it is a מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִין בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה — וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from telling the story to questioning what רבי אליעזר said in it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's description of festive eating as 'temporary life'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמחת יום טוב is a מצוה, so it should count as eternal life, not as something worth criticizing.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds that festive joy is optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר follows his own view: שמחת יום טוב is optional, not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, because he said that the joy of יום טוב is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רבי אליעזר has his own view about שמחת יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If festive eating were a required מצוה, criticizing it would make no sense. רבי אליעזר holds it is only optional, so learning Torah is the greater choice. That is why leaving the learning for food counts as 'temporary life.'

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean nobody holds there is a מצוה of שמחת יום טוב. It is only רבי אליעזר's view, and the next step shows רבי יהושע disagreeing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning,
for he said: the joy of the festival is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The speaker is shown to follow his own known position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees שמחת יום טוב is a required מצוה, so רבי אליעזר's criticism makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds it is optional, so choosing food over learning is choosing the lesser path.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves רבי אליעזר's view: a person spends יום טוב either eating and drinking or learning. רבי יהושע says to split the day in half.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, a person has nothing to do on יום טוב except either eat and drink, or sit and learn. רבי יהושע says: divide it, half for ה' and half for yourselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that רבי אליעזר really holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows a person to give the whole day to eating, so eating is allowed but not required. That fits calling it 'optional.' רבי יהושע disagrees and says every person should split the day, so some festive enjoyment is part of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא (brings a source as proof)
half for ה' and half for you

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person has nothing on a festival
except either eating and drinking,
or sitting and learning.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: divide it:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the day of יום טוב.

phrases.english: half for ה', and half for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in Step 18 that רבי אליעזר holds שמחת יום טוב is optional.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that שמחת יום טוב is optional
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says the day may be spent entirely on eating or entirely on learning, against רבי יהושע who says to split it
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the well-known מחלוקת about how a person should divide יום טוב between learning and festive enjoyment.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both views come from the same two פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows that both תנאים worked from the same pair of פסוקים: one says the day is 'for ה',' the other says it is 'for you.' He then asks how they fit together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same verses. One פסוק says 'an assembly for ה' your God,' and one פסוק says 'it shall be an assembly for you.' How do these fit together?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finds the source of the מחלוקת: two פסוקים that seem to point in opposite directions. His question 'how so?' sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes the day sound like it is all for serving ה'. The other makes it sound like it is for the people's own celebration. Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע are answering this same contradiction. They answer it in different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: they learned from the same verse(s)
how so? how do these fit together?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded the same verse.
phrases.notes: He means the same pair of פסוקים, which both of them read and explained.

phrases.english: One verse says:
"An assembly for ה' your God,"
and one verse says:
"It shall be an assembly for you."
How so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the source in the פסוקים for the מחלוקת quoted in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת comes from two פסוקים: one calls the day 'for ה',' and the other calls it 'for you.'

steps.title: Either all one way, or split in half
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוקים as a choice: the whole day for ה' or the whole day for you. רבי יהושע reads them as a split: half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: either all of it for ה', or all of it for you. רבי יהושע holds: divide it, half for ה' and half for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers his own question and explains how each תנא makes the two פסוקים fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the two פסוקים are two choices, and a person may pick either one for the whole day. For רבי יהושע, both פסוקים must be kept on the same day, so the day is split. This explains why רבי אליעזר can call eating optional.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole day

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the whole day for ה' or the whole day for you, so festive eating is optional. רבי יהושע: split the day, half learning and half festive enjoyment. Both come from the same two פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם.
phrases.english: either all of it for ה', or all of it for you.
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
Divide it: half for ה' and half for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'הא כיצד' question of Step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר reads the two פסוקים as a choice between giving the whole day to ה' or the whole day to yourself. That is why festive eating is optional for him. רבי יהושע requires splitting the day in half.

steps.title: What does 'for whoever has nothing prepared' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'לאין נכון לו' in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'to him for whom nothing is prepared'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a phrase from the פסוק in נחמיה. This sets up רב חסדא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the people to send portions to whoever has nothing prepared. It is not clear who that person is, or why he has nothing ready, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: to the one who has nothing prepared

phrases.english: What is 'to him for whom nothing is prepared'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the מחלוקת between the תנאים to explaining another phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the person 'for whom nothing is prepared'?

steps.title: רב חסדא: someone who did not make an עירוב תבשילין
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the phrase refers to someone who did not set up עירובי תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it means someone who did not put down an עירוב תבשילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The person 'with nothing prepared' is someone who did not make an עירוב תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב תבשילין, a person may not cook on יום טוב for the שבת that comes right after it. So he has no food ready for שבת, and others should send him food.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who explains the phrase
food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
To one who did not put down an eruv tavshilin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to someone who did not make an עירוב תבשילין and so has no food for שבת.

steps.title: Second version: only someone who could not make one
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב חסדא limits the phrase to someone who had no chance to make an עירוב. Someone who could have made one but did not is called negligent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: it means someone who was not able to put down an עירוב תבשילין. But someone who was able to and did not is negligent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב חסדא's answer. This version is narrower about who should be helped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, anyone without an עירוב is included. In this version, only someone who could not make one, for example because of a situation beyond his control, is the person the פסוק means. Someone who simply skipped it is a פושע, so the פסוק is not talking about him.

keyTerms.meaning: some say (another version of the statement)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions belong to רב חסדא. The difference is only about the person who could have made an עירוב but did not.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין,
phrases.english: One who was not able to put down an eruv tavshilin,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
phrases.english: but one who was able to put down an eruv tavshilin
and did not put it down, he is negligent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, narrower version of רב חסדא's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only someone who could not make an עירוב is meant. Someone who neglected to make one is a פושע.

steps.title: What does 'the joy of ה' is your strength' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about another phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'for the joy of ה' is your strength'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the end of the same פסוק. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious how joy can be someone's strength. The גמרא wants to know what this phrase is teaching.

phrases.english: What is 'for the joy of the Lord is your strength'?
phrases.notes: נחמיה 8:10, the same פסוק as before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'the joy of ה' is your strength' teach?

steps.title: Borrow on My account, and I will repay
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, explains that הקב"ה tells us to borrow if needed to honor the day, and He will repay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון: הקב"ה said to ישראל, 'My children, borrow on My account, make קידוש for the day, and trust in Me. I will pay it back.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the phrase. A person should not hold back from honoring שבת and יום טוב because he lacks money, since הקב"ה promises to repay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'joy of ה'' is the joy of the holy day, and it is 'your strength' because הקב"ה backs the expense. This turns the פסוק into a promise: money spent on קדושת היום will be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי

steps.whatToRemember: Spending to honor שבת and יום טוב is backed by הקב"ה's promise to repay.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
My children, borrow on My account,
and sanctify the holiness of the day,
phrases.notes: He means making קידוש over wine for שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: and trust in Me, and I will repay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב"ה promises to repay what is borrowed to honor the day.

steps.title: Plant an אדר tree to protect your property
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching from the same chain: whoever wants his property to last should plant an אדר tree, based on the word 'אדיר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון: Whoever wants his property to last should plant an אדר tree on it, as it says, 'ה' on high is mighty (אדיר).'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted this chain of teachers, it adds another teaching from them. This one is about protecting property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a play on words: אדר sounds like אדיר, 'mighty'. Like ה' who is mighty and lasting, the אדר tree gives the property strength and lasting power.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Shimon:
One who wants his properties to last
should plant an eder tree among them,
as it is stated: 'The Lord on high is mighty.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:4. The proof rests on אדיר sounding like אדר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching because it has the same chain of teachers as step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting an אדר tree helps a person's property last.

steps.title: Another reason: the tree's name means lasting
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: the name אדרא itself hints that it lasts for generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or: the אדר works just as its name says. As people say: why is it called אדרא? Because it lasts for generations and generations (דרי דרי).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second source for the same idea. This time the source is the tree's own name, not a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a word-play with אדיר, the name אדרא is read as related to דרי, 'generations'. People said this because the tree lives a very long time, so the property keeps an owner's mark for generations.

phrases.english: Alternatively, the eder is like its name,
as people say:
What is 'adra'? That it lasts for generations and generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for the same teaching as step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree's name shows that it lasts for generations.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the teaching about the אדר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that a field with an אדר tree is protected from being stolen, and its fruit is kept safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: a field with an אדר tree in it is not stolen or taken by force, and its fruit is kept safe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the teaching about the אדר tree. This closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows the practical benefit of the tree: the field is protected from thieves and from people who take land by force, and its produce is preserved. This supports the idea that an אדר helps property last.

keyTerms.meaning: it is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
taken by force (often with some payment)

steps.whatToRemember: The אדר tree protects a person's field, both because of the פסוק 'אדיר' and because its name means 'lasting for generations', and a ברייתא supports this.

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
A field that has an eder tree in it
is not stolen and is not taken by force,
and its fruit is kept safe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the teaching in steps 27-28.
steps.raayaObject: That an אדר tree helps a person's property last.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a field with an אדר is not stolen or taken by force, and its fruit is kept safe.

steps.title: רב תחליפא introduces a teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names רב תחליפא, brother of רבנאי חוזאה, as the one who taught the next teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא, the brother of רבנאי חוזאה, taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us who is about to teach, and the teaching itself comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תני tells us the teaching is a learned tradition (a ברייתא), not just one אמורא's own opinion. After the side point about the אדר tree, this opening brings us back to the main theme from step 26: spending money to honor the day.

keyTerms.meaning: "Taught". Used to bring a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
"From חוזאי", a place name used to tell this teacher apart from others

phrases.english: Rav Taḥlifa taught
the brother of Ravnai Ḥoza'a:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבְנַאי חוֹזָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about the אדר tree (steps 27-29) and goes back to the theme of spending to honor יום טוב from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only names the teacher, and the content of his ברייתא comes next.
